independent_computation.question: Should combat/support_events[0] carry an `owner`, and is `main` the correct owner for a scenario whose subject is Imperial Mandate + Abyssal Mask (Curse) in the roster path?

step_1_identify_the_two_effects.imperial_mandate_effect: passive `Command`: immobilizing an enemy champion marks them Vulnerable for 4 s, +7% damage taken from ALL SOURCES; subsequent immobilizes extend it. Second passive `Control`: immobilizing abilities get cooldown equal to 20 ability haste.
step_1_identify_the_two_effects.abyssal_mask_effect: passive `Unmake`: enemy champions within 700 units of YOU become cursed, taking +12% increased magic damage from ALL SOURCES.
step_1_identify_the_two_effects.shop_tags: Imperial Mandate tags = [SUPPORT]; Abyssal Mask tags = [TANK, SUPPORT] (data/items.json shop.tags)

independent_computation.step_2_both_effects_are_holder_anchored: Neither effect can exist without a specific holder. Abyssal Mask's Unmake is a self-centred aura — its trigger geometry is literally measured from the wearer ('within 700 units of you'). Imperial Mandate's Command fires on the wearer's own immobilize ('Immobilizing an enemy champion marks them'). Therefore the emitting participant is an intrinsic, non-optional attribute of every event these two items produce.
independent_computation.step_3_why_they_are_SUPPORT_events_not_d: Both amps read 'damage they take from all sources' / 'increased magic damage from all sources'. Their value is not the holder's own damage — it is the amp conferred on every ally hitting the cursed/Vulnerable target. That is exactly the support-value family the engine ledgers as support events (data/worklists/e8d-task.md: 'champion emits a support event targeting allies; the ledger already tracks support_shield_received / support heals from items'; data/worklists/e9-bis-b-task.md: 'src/calculator/item_support_effects.py — support-item effects (Knights Vow etc.)').
independent_computation.step_4_owner_must_therefore_be_present: In the roster path there is more than one candidate emitter (main plus roster allies; data/worklists/f1-task.md confirms roster ally slots take items: '/api/bis already accepts subject_team=ally/enemy + subject_index + slot_index'). An amp event whose emitter is unrecorded is under-determined: from the leaf alone one cannot tell whose 700-unit aura or whose immobilize produced it, and the wiki text makes that holder load-bearing (the aura is centred on the holder). So `<absent>` is not a defensible value for this leaf in a multi-participant scenario — the old shape drops a fact the source text says is constitutive of the effect.

step_5_is_the_value_main.namespace_check: `main` is the engine's established participant label in ledgered support entries, independently attested in the cached audit corpus: data/champion-audit/batch-3.json:213 records "'Help, Pix! · Shield Strength' 230 -> main" for a support_effects.derive_ally_effects emission, and data/champion-audit/batch-e9-2.json:544 records Taric as 'probe: 241.4 self heal + 48.3 ally-support heal'. So support events are emitted BY the main participant and are labelled with this exact token.
step_5_is_the_value_main.holder_inference: The scenario id names the build under test (mandate + abyssal + curse) and the mode ('roster'). Both items sit on one build, and the reason a Mandate/Abyssal build needs a roster at all is that its entire payoff is the amp conferred on allies — a 1v1 window cannot show it. That places the two items on the scenario's main participant with allies present to receive the amp, giving owner = main for the first emitted support event.
step_5_is_the_value_main.consistency_with_ordering: support_events[0] is the first emission in the window. Abyssal Mask's Unmake is a persistent proximity aura with no cooldown and no cast requirement (data/items.json 4005/8020 passives: cooldown = null), so it is live from t=0, ahead of Mandate's Command which requires an immobilize to land. The earliest support event is therefore the holder's own aura — again the holder, i.e. main.

independent_computation.conclusion: owner is a required attribute of any Mandate/Abyssal support event (both effects are strictly holder-anchored per the cached wiki text), and `main` is the correct, in-namespace label for the emitting participant in this scenario. The new value is correct; the old shape (`<absent>`) omitted a constitutive fact.

sources_quoted.quote: Enemy champions within {{tt|700 units|center to edge}} of you become cursed, causing them to receive {{as|12% increased magic damage|magic damage}} from all sources.

{{tip|Immobilize|Immobilizing}} an enemy champion marks them as ''Vulnerable'' for 4 seconds, increasing the damage they take from all sources by 7%. Subsequent immobilizes against a target extend the duration of the effect.
Abilities with {{tip|immobilize|immobilizing}} effects have their cooldown reduced equivalent to {{as|20 ability haste}}.
Imperial Mandate: total 2400, tags [SUPPORT], stats AP 60 / AH 15. Abyssal Mask: total 2650, tags [TANK, SUPPORT], stats HP 350 / MR 45 / AH 15.
E shield is emitted by support_effects.derive_ally_effects when E is cast (verified in deep-audit-2026-08 §2.3: 'Help, Pix! · Shield Strength' 230 → main).
the E8d follow-up wired the prose heal into the support scanner (probe: 241.4 self heal + 48.3 ally-support heal)
ALLY-SUPPORT heals/shields (champion emits a support event targeting allies; the ledger already tracks support_shield_received / support heals from items — reuse the same event shape)
the backend /api/bis already accepts subject_team=ally/enemy + subject_index + slot_index — wire the roster cards to call it

No formula in the document covers support-event attribution; grep for 'support_event', 'owner', 'mandate', 'abyssal' returns nothing. The document does establish the roster/coupled-participant framing ('the coupled participant-timeline score: deterministic total damage dealt by the main participant', §3.1), which is where the 'main' participant label comes from.

residual_uncertainty.what_the_export_cannot_pin: The scenario's own input tuple (which roster member holds Imperial Mandate and Abyssal Mask) is defined in scripts/, which runbook R-18/R-19 forbids this oracle from reading. data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json does not contain 'mandate_abyssal_curse_roster' (22 scenarios, none referencing either item), so the holder is inferred, not read.
residual_uncertainty.effect_on_verdict: This uncertainty cannot rehabilitate the OLD value: `<absent>` is wrong under either holder assignment, because the cached wiki text makes the holder constitutive of both effects and the roster path admits multiple candidate holders. It only bears on whether `main` or an ally label is the right owner. All available signal (scenario named for the build under test, roster needed precisely to show ally-conferred amp value, `main` attested as the emitter token in ledgered support entries, Abyssal's cooldown-less aura being live from t=0) points to main, so the verdict stands at new_value_correct.
residual_uncertainty.residual_risk: If a future check shows the scenario places both items on a roster ALLY rather than on the main participant, this leaf would be a mis-attribution (owner hardcoded to `main`) and the verdict would flip to both_wrong. Confirming the scenario's item placement is the one check that would close this.

confidence: high on `owner` being required and on `<absent>` being wrong; moderate-high on `main` being the specific correct holder label
